To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the metabolic and regulatory systems of E. coli are complex and can be modeled using dynamic modeling.

we constructed a dynamic simulation model of the metabolic and regulatory systems of Escherichiae coli for amino acid production and that we used it to study the effect of carbon sources and genetic changes on glutamate production.
we constructed a dynamic simulation model for E. coli metabolic and regulatory networks that can be used for the design of metabolic and genetic engineering of amino acid production.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a dynamic model of Eschericia coli metabolic and regulatory processes for amino-acid fermentation, and with the application of the model in the improvement of amino-acid production by Eschericia coli.
the construction of a practical dynamic-simulated system that can model metabolic and regulatory processes in E. coli.
a new approach for the design of metabolic and regulative networks in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed an in silico tool that could be used in the rational design of metabolic and/or regulatory processes.
we have constructed a dynamic simulation system that can be used for modeling the metabolic and regulatory systems of Escherichiae coli for amino acid production.
the simulation model could function a new tool for rational design of metabolic and regulation network in the production of amino acid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have constructed a practical dynamic-simulated system for the production of primary metabolic compounds.

we have constructed an Escherichia Coli model that could be used to simulate the production of amino acids, such as glutamate, by batch fermentation, and to predict the effects of genetic modifications on the metabolic and regulatory networks.
we constructed a practical dynamic-simulated system that can model metabolic and regulatory processes of primary metabolite production in E. coli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a model that includes both the metabolic and regulatory parts can be used to simulate the production of primary and secondary metabolites by transient batch-culture.
a model can be developed that can be used to predict the effects of changes in the metabolic network and regulatory network.
the model could serve as a new tool to design and improve the metabolic networks of E. coli for the production of primary products.
